title: How many CLE and ethics hours do attorneys need in the largest US states?
description: Mandatory CLE for attorneys in NY, CA, TX, FL, IL and PA: total hours, ethics hours, special topics, reporting cycles and carryover, from official rules.
shortAnswer: Mandatory continuing legal education (CLE) is set state by state. As at November 2026, New York requires 24 credits every two years, California 25 hours every three years, Texas 15 hours a year, Florida 30 hours every three years, Illinois 30 hours every two years and Pennsylvania 12 hours a year. Each state also sets a minimum in ethics or professional responsibility, from 2 hours a year in Pennsylvania to 6 hours per period in Illinois.
keyTakeaways: There is no national CLE rule. Each state supreme court or bar sets its own hours, cycle, special topics and carryover limits.
Ethics minimums differ: New York 4 per biennial cycle, California 4 per three-year period, Texas 3 a year, Florida 5 per three-year cycle, Illinois 6 per two-year period and Pennsylvania 2 a year.

Several states mandate specific topics: New York requires diversity and cybersecurity credits, California requires bias, competence, technology and civility hours, and Florida requires 3 technology hours.
Cycles are tied to different anchors: birthdays in New York and Texas, last names in California and Illinois, and assigned compliance groups in Pennsylvania.
Carryover ranges from none in California to 15 hours in Texas, so multi-state firms cannot apply one rule to all lawyers.
jurisdiction: United States (New York, California, Texas, Florida, Illinois, Pennsylvania)
regulator: State supreme courts and their CLE boards: New York CLE Board, State Bar of California, State Bar of Texas MCLE Department, The Florida Bar, Illinois MCLE Board, Pennsylvania CLE Board

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: Figures were read on each state's rule or regulator page as at November 2026. California is mid-way through a deadline realignment, and Texas revised its MCLE Regulations effective April 24, 2026. Attorneys admitted in other states should check those states' own rules.

New York requires 24 credit hours per biennial reporting cycle under [22 NYCRR 1500.22](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/new-york/22-NYCRR-1500.22). The rule requires "at least four (4) credit hours of which shall be in ethics and professionalism, at least one (1) credit hour of which shall be in diversity, inclusion and elimination of bias, and at least one (1) credit hour of which shall be in cybersecurity, privacy and data protection."

Up to 3 credits of cybersecurity, privacy and data protection ethics can count toward the 4 hour ethics requirement. The cycle is linked to the attorney's biennial registration statement, and an attorney who earns more than 24 credits may carry over a maximum of 6 credits to the next cycle. Credit is also available for teaching, judging law competitions, publications and qualifying pro bono work.

California requires 25 hours of Minimum Continuing Legal Education (MCLE) in each three-year compliance period, and at least 12.5 must be participatory. The [State Bar of California MCLE requirements page](https://www.calbar.ca.gov/legal-professionals/maintaining-compliance/mcle/mcle-requirements) lists at least 4 hours of legal ethics, 2 hours on elimination of bias including 1 hour on implicit bias and bias-reducing strategies (Business and Professions Code section 6070.5), 2 hours of competence including 1 hour on prevention and detection of substance use and mental health issues, 1 hour on technology in the practice of law, and 1 hour on civility.

Compliance groups are fixed by the first letter of the attorney's last name and the State Bar is realigning deadlines. Group 3 (N to Z) had a single 38-month cycle ending March 29, 2026; Group 2 (H to M) has one ending March 29, 2027, with reports due March 30, 2027; Group 1 (A to G) runs March 30, 2025 to March 29, 2028. After the extended cycle each group returns to a standard 36-month cycle. Up to half of a proportionally reduced requirement may be self-study.

Texas requires 15 hours of CLE every MCLE compliance year, including at least 3 hours of legal ethics or professional responsibility. Under section 3.1 of the [Texas MCLE Regulations](https://www.texasbar.com/AM/Template.cfm?Section=MCLE_Rules1&Template=/CM/ContentDisplay.cfm&ContentID=71381), effective April 24, 2026, at least 12 of the 15 hours must be accredited CLE activities. Section 3.2 requires 2 of the 3 ethics hours to be accredited, and allows 1 to be self-study.

The compliance year follows the attorney's birth month, and an automatic grace period runs to the end of the birth month before penalties apply. Self-study is capped at 3 hours per compliance year. Excess hours, including ethics hours, may be carried forward to the next year up to a maximum of 15 (section 3.3, citing Article XII, Section 6E of the State Bar Rules).

sections.heading: What do Florida, Illinois and Pennsylvania require?

blocks.text: **Florida** requires a minimum of 30 credit hours every three years under Rule 6-10 of the Rules Regulating The Florida Bar. The [Florida Bar CLE FAQ](https://www.floridabar.org/member/cle/general-cle-info-and-requirements/cler-faq/) states that at least 3 hours must be approved technology programs, and at least 5 must be legal ethics, professionalism, substance abuse or mental health and wellness, including the mandatory 2 credit Florida Legal Professionalism course in each reporting cycle. Members receive an email at least three months before the end of their cycle.

**Illinois** Supreme Court [Rule 794](https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/rules/supreme-court-rules?a=vii) requires 30 hours in each two-year reporting period ending June 30. Lawyers with last names A to M start periods on July 1 of even-numbered years, and N to Z on July 1 of odd-numbered years. At least 6 hours must be in professionalism, civility, legal ethics, sexual harassment prevention, diversity and inclusion, or mental health and substance abuse, including at least 1 hour each of diversity and inclusion and mental health and substance abuse unless the lawyer completes the yearlong Lawyer-to-Lawyer Mentoring Program. Up to 10 hours may carry over.

**Pennsylvania** requires 12 credit hours a year, of which at least 2 must be ethics, during the compliance period for the lawyer's permanently assigned compliance group, according to the [Pennsylvania CLE Board FAQ](https://www.pacle.org/faq). An initial $100 late compliance fee applies if the 12 hours are not completed by the deadline, and continued non-compliance leads to a Supreme Court order of administrative suspension.

sections.heading: How should a multi-state firm track CLE obligations?

blocks.text: Track each attorney against each state of admission separately, because cycles, ethics minimums and topic mandates do not line up. A lawyer admitted in New York and California, for example, needs diversity and cybersecurity credits on a two-year birthday cycle and bias, competence, technology and civility hours on a three-year last-name cycle.

blocks.text: The structure used for a [training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) works well: one row per attorney and state, one column per required category, with cycle end dates. Australian practitioners and firms with offices there can compare the [NSW solicitor CPD requirements](/regulations/nsw-solicitor-cpd-requirements). Many firms also coordinate CLE with mandatory workplace training such as [state sexual harassment training](/regulations/state-sexual-harassment-training-requirements), since some states credit bias or harassment topics toward CLE.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each internal course to the state categories it can satisfy, such as New York ethics and professionalism or California civility, before content is written, so firms can design one session to serve several states. Completion records are then held against each attorney's state cycles, ready for the evidence firms in the [professional services sector](/industries/professional-services) need at reporting time.

faqs.q: Which of these states requires the most CLE per year?
faqs.a: Texas and Illinois both average 15 hours a year (15 annually in Texas, 30 per two years in Illinois), ahead of New York at 12 a year averaged, Pennsylvania at 12, Florida at 10 averaged and California at about 8.3 averaged.

faqs.q: Does New York accept cybersecurity ethics toward the ethics requirement?
faqs.a: Yes. 22 NYCRR 1500.22(a) lets attorneys apply up to 3 credit hours of cybersecurity, privacy and data protection ethics to the 4 credit hour ethics and professionalism requirement, in addition to the separate 1 hour cybersecurity requirement.

faqs.q: Can CLE be completed entirely online?
faqs.a: It depends on the state. California requires at least half of the 25 hours to be participatory, Texas caps self-study at 3 hours a year, and Illinois requires interactivity in every approved delivery method. Pennsylvania distance learning hours do not carry forward.

faqs.q: Do newly admitted attorneys follow the same rules?
faqs.a: No. Each state has separate requirements for newly admitted attorneys, such as Texas's initial 24-month compliance year, Florida's Basic Skills Course Requirement and Illinois Rule 793. This page covers experienced attorneys.
